name: Montrose
tagline: Bungalows, bookshops and Houston's creative core
description: Montrose is a low-rise grid of 1920s bungalows and small apartment courts west of downtown, historically the city's gay and artistic quarter. Westheimer Road runs through it lined with vintage shops, tattoo studios, cocktail bars and coffee houses. The Menil Collection and Rothko Chapel sit here, free and surrounded by lawns.
bestFor: Nomads who want the most walkable, characterful part of a very car-dependent city.
pros: Genuinely walkable to bars, cafes and galleries
Free world-class art at the Menil campus
Central, so short drives everywhere else
cons: Rents have climbed sharply as it gentrified
Old bungalows mean patchy insulation and AC bills
Street parking is tight on weekend nights

name: Midtown
tagline: Apartment blocks on the light rail, best value central
description: Midtown fills the gap between downtown and the Museum District with mid-rise apartment complexes, surface lots and a dense strip of bars along Bagby and Gray. The METRORail Red Line runs straight through it, connecting downtown, the Museum District and the Medical Center without a car. Units are newer and cheaper than Montrose.
bestFor: Anyone who wants a modern apartment, a gym in the building and no car payment.
pros: Light rail makes a car optional
Newer buildings with fast fibre and gyms
Cheaper per square foot than Montrose or the Heights
cons: Bar strip gets loud on weekend nights
Blocks of parking lots and little shade
Feels transient, thin on neighbourhood character

name: The Heights
tagline: Victorian porches and a bike trail into town
description: Houston Heights is a historic district north-west of downtown, laid out on a raised grid with Victorian and Craftsman houses, wide esplanades and mature oaks. The Heights Hike and Bike Trail cuts through toward downtown, and 19th Street carries antique shops, bakeries and taprooms. Zoning-free Houston has filled the gaps with new townhomes.
bestFor: Longer stays where a quiet, green, family-flavoured neighbourhood beats nightlife.
pros: Leafy, quiet streets with real character
Strong cafe, bakery and brewery scene
cons: Mostly whole houses, few short-term options
You will need a car for most errands
Prices now rival the most expensive inner loop areas

name: Downtown
description: Downtown is the office core, a grid of glass towers linked by seven miles of air-conditioned pedestrian tunnels, with Discovery Green park, three pro sports venues and the theatre district at its edges. Converted and purpose-built residential towers offer studios with rooftop pools, and it empties out considerably after work hours.
bestFor: Short stays or event trips where being able to walk to everything downtown is the point.
pros: Walk to theatre, sports and the convention centre
Tunnel system beats the summer heat
Rail and bus lines converge here
cons: Very quiet and empty on evenings and weekends
Few grocery stores or everyday shops
Parking and building fees add up fast

name: EaDo
tagline: Warehouse conversions east of the tracks
description: East Downtown is a former industrial and Vietnamese commercial strip now full of murals, breweries, soccer-night crowds at Shell Energy Stadium and warehouse lofts converted into apartments. It sits one rail stop from downtown and still has raw edges: empty lots, freight tracks and blocks that go dark early.
bestFor: Nomads chasing space and lower rent inside the loop who do not mind a rough-edged block or two.
pros: Larger lofts for less than Montrose money
One rail stop or a walk from downtown
Breweries, murals and live music venues
cons: Patchy street lighting, quiet after dark
Freight trains cross and block roads
Few grocery stores within walking distance
